📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough The PR upgrades the ACP SDK dependency and refactors session management, recorder lifecycle, and tool call tracking. It introduces ACP session modes with fixed mode IDs, improves resource cleanup via session lifecycle management, migrates todo-update recording from command layer to web server, and enhances tool call identification with concurrent-safe state mapping and improved approval matching. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**ACP SDK Upgrade**
`go.mod`|Bumped `github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk` from v0.6.3 to v0.12.0. Added direct requirements for `github.com/mdp/qrterminal/v3` and `tinygo.org/x/bluetooth`, removed indirect dependency `github.com/mattn/go-colorable`.| |**Session Lifecycle & Mode Support**
`internal/command/acp.go`, `internal/session/session.go`|Added fixed ACP session modes (agent, plan) with mode state tracking in `acpSession`. Implemented `SetSessionMode` for validating, recording, and switching active prompts/tools with agent rebuild. Added `acpSession.Close()` for resource cleanup. Introduced `broadcastSlashCommands` to advertise skill-based commands. Added `ListAllSessions()` function to read shared session index from disk.| |**Recorder Management & Todo Snapshot Recording**
`internal/command/web.go`, `internal/web/server.go`|Removed todo recording callback from command layer. Migrated todo-update recording to `NewServer`, wiring `cfg.TodoStore.OnUpdate` to record snapshots into `s.recorder` with read-lock synchronization. Refactored `handleNewSession` to compute todo updates under lock, then apply them unlocked to avoid deadlocks. Updated session lifecycle to close all recorders on connection shutdown and previous instances on `LoadSession` replacement.| |**Tool Call Tracking & Approval Matching**
`internal/handler/acp.go`|Replaced single `activeToolCall` field with concurrent-safe maps (`einoToACP`, `toolArgs`, `pendingApprovals`) to associate Eino tool call IDs with ACP ToolCallIds. Extended `OnToolCall` and `OnToolResult` signatures to accept Eino tool call ID. Implemented approval matching by `(ToolName, ToolArgs)` with FIFO fallback. Added diff-based update content for edit/write operations and improved error logging via `logACPError` helper.| ## Sequence Diagram ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant ACPAgent as ACP Agent participant SessionMgr as Session Manager participant PromptMgr as Prompt Manager participant ToolMgr as Tool Manager Client->>ACPAgent: SetSessionMode(newModeId) activate ACPAgent ACPAgent->>SessionMgr: ValidateMode(newModeId) SessionMgr-->>ACPAgent: Valid ACPAgent->>SessionMgr: RecordModeChange(newModeId) ACPAgent->>PromptMgr: GetModePrompt(newModeId) PromptMgr-->>ACPAgent: SystemPrompt ACPAgent->>ToolMgr: GetModeToolset(newModeId) ToolMgr-->>ACPAgent: Tools[] ACPAgent->>ACPAgent: RebuildAgent(prompt, tools) deactivate ACPAgent ACPAgent->>Client: CurrentModeUpdate(newModeId) ``` ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~75 minutes ## Possibly related PRs - **cnjack/jcode#28**: Modifies ACP session lifecycle, resume logic, and recorder/session state management patterns similar to this PR's refactoring of session initialization and closing behavior. ## Poem > 🐰 *Modes hop and switch, recorders align,* > *Tool calls now tracked with IDs so fine,* > *Resources cleaned when sessions depart,* > *Approval queues match each agent's art!* ✨

**Actionable comments posted: 2** > [!CAUTION] > Some comments are outside the diff and can’t be posted inline due to platform limitations. > > > >
> ⚠️ Outside diff range comments (1)
> >
> internal/handler/acp.go (1)
> > `133-214`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ > > **Auto-approved tool calls leak `pendingApprovals` entries and can poison the FIFO fallback.** > > `OnToolCall` unconditionally appends to `pendingApprovals` (line 140), but only `RequestApproval` removes entries. For any tool that is auto-approved (read-only tools, safe `execute` prefixes, or when `AutoApprove`/session-auto is set), `h.RequestApproval` is never invoked, so the entry stays forever. Two consequences: > > 1. Unbounded slice growth across a long session. > 2. If a later mutating call doesn't match by `(toolName, toolArgs)` exactly (e.g., the approval middleware re-serializes args with different whitespace/key order), the FIFO fallback at lines 248–251 pops a **stale auto-approved entry's `acpID`** and sends the permission request with the wrong `ToolCallId` — reintroducing the exact class of bug this PR is fixing. > > `OnToolResult` already knows the `acpID` via `einoToACP`; it should also purge the matching pendingApprovals entry. > >
> 🔒 Proposed fix: remove pendingApprovals entry on tool result > > ```diff > func (h *ACPHandler) OnToolResult(name, output, einoToolCallID string, err error) { > h.mu.Lock() > id := h.einoToACP[einoToolCallID] > cachedArgs := h.toolArgs[id] > delete(h.einoToACP, einoToolCallID) > delete(h.toolArgs, id) > + // Drop any still-queued approval entry for this ACP id (e.g. auto-approved > + // tools never go through RequestApproval and would otherwise leak and > + // poison the FIFO fallback on the next approval request). > + if id != "" { > + for i, p := range h.pendingApprovals { > + if p.acpID == id { > + h.pendingApprovals = append(h.pendingApprovals[:i], h.pendingApprovals[i+1:]...) > + break > + } > + } > + } > h.mu.Unlock() > ``` >
> >
> 🤖 Prompt for AI Agents > > ``` > Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. > > In `@internal/handler/acp.go` around lines 133 - 214, OnToolCall always appends a > pendingApproval to h.pendingApprovals but auto-approved calls never invoke > RequestApproval, causing leaked/stale entries; modify OnToolResult to remove the > pendingApproval whose acpID matches the id resolved from h.einoToACP so the FIFO > fallback can't pop stale entries. Specifically, in ACPHandler.OnToolResult > (which already looks up id via h.einoToACP and deletes that map entry), also > scan and delete the matching pendingApproval element from h.pendingApprovals > (the slice of pendingApproval structs) before unlocking or continuing; this > ensures entries added by OnToolCall are cleaned up when the tool result arrives > and prevents unbounded growth and wrong ToolCallId reuse. > ``` > >
> >
> >
🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
internal/handler/acp.go (1)
`122-131`: **`parseRawInput` string fallback will still produce a JSON-encoded string, re-triggering the original symptom.** If `argsJSON` isn't valid JSON, returning the raw string causes the SDK to serialize `RawInput` as a JSON *string* (exactly the "double-escaped string" case the PR set out to eliminate). In practice Eino args should always be valid JSON, but a malformed provider response would silently revert to the old behavior. Consider returning `nil` (or logging) on parse failure so the inspector surfaces the problem instead of masking it.
✨ Proposed fallback ```diff var obj map[string]any if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(argsJSON), &obj); err != nil { - return argsJSON // fallback to string if not valid JSON + config.Logger().Printf("[acp-handler] parseRawInput: invalid JSON args: %v", err) + return nil } return obj ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@internal/handler/acp.go` around lines 122 - 131, The parseRawInput function currently returns the original argsJSON string on JSON unmarshal failure, which causes the SDK to re-serialize RawInput as a JSON string and reintroduce the double-escaped symptom; change parseRawInput to return nil on unmarshal error (and optionally log the parse error) instead of returning argsJSON so malformed provider responses surface as a missing/invalid RawInput; update the function parseRawInput to perform json.Unmarshal into obj and on error call the logger (if available) and return nil. ```
🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. Inline comments: In `@internal/command/acp.go`: - Around line 506-552: The code holds sess.mu via defer sess.mu.Unlock() while calling a.conn.SessionUpdate which can block; remove the defer and instead unlock the session mutex immediately after mutating session state (after setting sess.mode, calling sess.rec.RecordModeChange, and assigning sess.ag when sess.createAgent returns) so that the critical section ends before calling a.conn.SessionUpdate; specifically, replace the defer pattern around sess.mu.Lock() with an explicit sess.mu.Unlock() right after the agent recreation/logging block (leave locking for the mutations of sess.mode, sess.rec, sess.ag), then call a.conn.SessionUpdate without holding sess.mu. - Around line 556-576: In ListSessions (func (a *acpAgent) ListSessions) you must avoid returning a pointer to an empty string for the optional Title field; change the construction of acp.SessionInfo so that Title is nil when m.Title == "" and only set to &m.Title when non-empty (i.e. if m.Title == "" { Title: nil } else { Title: &m.Title }). This ensures the ACP optional Title pointer follows the SDK convention and lets clients render their "no title" placeholder. --- Outside diff comments: In `@internal/handler/acp.go`: - Around line 133-214: OnToolCall always appends a pendingApproval to h.pendingApprovals but auto-approved calls never invoke RequestApproval, causing leaked/stale entries; modify OnToolResult to remove the pendingApproval whose acpID matches the id resolved from h.einoToACP so the FIFO fallback can't pop stale entries. Specifically, in ACPHandler.OnToolResult (which already looks up id via h.einoToACP and deletes that map entry), also scan and delete the matching pendingApproval element from h.pendingApprovals (the slice of pendingApproval structs) before unlocking or continuing; this ensures entries added by OnToolCall are cleaned up when the tool result arrives and prevents unbounded growth and wrong ToolCallId reuse. --- Nitpick comments: In `@internal/handler/acp.go`: - Around line 122-131: The parseRawInput function currently returns the original argsJSON string on JSON unmarshal failure, which causes the SDK to re-serialize RawInput as a JSON string and reintroduce the double-escaped symptom; change parseRawInput to return nil on unmarshal error (and optionally log the parse error) instead of returning argsJSON so malformed provider responses surface as a missing/invalid RawInput; update the function parseRawInput to perform json.Unmarshal into obj and on error call the logger (if available) and return nil. ```
